basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 5-6.' and it opens 'VERS. 5, 6.-- Suspice coelum, et numera stellas, si potes. Et dixit ei: Sic erit semen'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 5, 6.-- Suspice coelum, et numera stellas, si potes. Et dixit ei: Sic erit semen tuum. Unde in consequentibus dicit: Sicut stellae coeli, et sicut arena quae est in littore maris. In stellis coeli pauciores, firmiores, clariores intelliguntur; in arena autem maritimi littoris magna multitudo infirmorum atque carnalium.
